v1.tie_policy: same-time ambiguity fails closed for sequential claims; deterministic content ordering is not asserted to be true arrival order

v2.tie_policy: timestamp_received orders observable replay; same-ms groups are ambiguous and must be batched/fail closed for within-group sequencing

ag6.tie_policy: same as V2; AG6 is independently captured but schema-compatible with PMXT V2

v3.tie_policy: sort by timestamp_received for observable-time approximation; never use file row order or sequence as a global event order
v3.witness_rule: source_witness/witness_set/arrival_skew are capture-provenance fields; absence on oldest V3 hours is expected and requires schema union-by-name

hard_fail_rules: No future snapshots or forward nearest-neighbour joins.
No use of V1 timestamp_created_at as observable time.
No use of V2/ag6/v3 exchange timestamp as the replay-observable ordering clock.
No use of V3 sequence as a global cross-witness ordering clock.
No interpretation of V3 physical file row order as live arrival order.
Same-time ambiguity fails closed when a claim requires within-timestamp sequence.
continuity_rule: Source-missing/zero-row hours break continuity. Features/targets crossing those holes must be invalidated rather than bridged.
